data.text:
According to NHK, JSDF🇯🇵 troops participating in Exercise Balikatan, including JS Ise and personnel from the Amphibious Rapid Deployment Brigade, have departed Sasebo Naval Base for the Philippines🇵🇭: https://t.co/JDNSaOF0Hh.

■Translation:
JGSDF Amphibious Rapid Deployment Brigade to Participate in Multinational Exercise; Departs Sasebo for the Philippines

It has been learned that the Japan Ground Self-Defense Force’s Amphibious Rapid Deployment Brigade (ARDB), headquartered in Sasebo City, will for the first time participate in full-scale operations in a multinational joint exercise to be held in the Philippines from this month into next. On the 14th, personnel embarked on Maritime Self-Defense Force transport ships and other vessels and departed from Sasebo Base.

The exercise is the annual multinational drill “Balikatan,” hosted by the United States and the Philippines.

According to the JMOD, the JSDF have previously participated mainly as observers. However, this time, approximately 1,400 personnel will be dispatched from the Ground, Maritime, and Air Self-Defense Forces. Among them, the ARDB—based in Sasebo—will serve as one of the main units, conducting amphibious landing exercises.

Ahead of the deployment, at JMSDF Sasebo Base, AAV7 amphibious assault vehicles and personnel boarded transport ships and destroyers between the 12th and 13th. On the morning of the 14th, the vessels departed for the Philippines.

This exercise will also mark the first large-scale training involving coordination between the newly established JMSDF amphibious warfare unit—launched at Sasebo last month—and the ARDB. Cooperation between the JGSDF and JMSDF aimed at strengthening the defense of the Nansei Islands is now being fully developed with Sasebo as its hub.

[Background: Strengthening Japan–Philippines Cooperation]

According to the JMOD, Japan has been deepening security cooperation with the Philippines in recent years. Four years ago, the two countries held their first “2+2” meeting of foreign and defense ministers, where they expressed serious concerns over the situations in the East and South China Seas, with China in mind, and confirmed their intention to further strengthen security cooperation.

In addition, over the past decade, the Self-Defense Forces and the Philippine military have conducted continuous joint activities, including naval exercises and land-based disaster relief training. The entry into force of the Reciprocal Access Agreement (RAA) in September last year—facilitating smoother entry and exit procedures for joint exercises—has enabled more practical training involving the deployment of weapons.

Participation in this year’s “Balikatan” is also being conducted under the RAA framework. According to the Ministry of Defense, the ARDB will conduct amphibious landing exercises, while a JGSDF anti-ship missile unit is scheduled to carry out live-fire training in the Philippines for the first time.

[Full-Scale Integration of Ground–Maritime Cooperation]

This exercise also represents the first large-scale training involving coordination between the ARDB and a newly established MSDF unit, created this spring to strengthen the defense posture of the Nansei Islands.

The “Amphibious Mine Warfare Group” (informally known as the “Amphibious-Mine Warfare Group”), headquartered in Sasebo, was established during a major MSDF organizational reform last month. Its primary missions are amphibious operations—landing on and recapturing remote islands—and mine warfare, including the laying and clearance of naval mines.

In amphibious operations, close coordination with the ARDB is essential, which is one of the reasons cited by the Ministry of Defense for locating the new unit’s headquarters in Sasebo.

In this exercise, alongside the ARDB, the MSDF’s large helicopter destroyer Ise—effectively serving as the group’s flagship—and the transport ship Shimokita will participate. Cooperation between the Ground and Maritime Self-Defense Forces, aimed at strengthening the defense of the Nansei Islands, is now advancing in earnest with Sasebo as its operational hub.

Tinalakay na sa Senado sa ginanap na pagdinig ng Senate Committee on Public Order and Dangerous Drugs ngayong Miyerkules, Abril 15, ang panukalang batas na naglalayong itaas ang salary grades at iayon ang mga ranggo ng Bureau of Fire Protection (BFP) at Bureau of Jail Management and Penology (BJMP) sa kanilang mga counterpart sa Philippine National Police (PNP) at Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) kabilang ang usapin sa kinakailangang pondo at epekto nito sa retirement at pension obligations.

Ayon sa pahayag ng Department of Budget and Management (DBM), magkakaroon ito ng epekto sa pension requirements dahil sa indexation factor kung saan tumataas din ang pension kasabay ng pagtaas ng sahod ng mga personnel. | DZRH News
